Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 How To Play 1.1 Adding a Tile 1.2 Build Walkways 1.3 Drawing a Tile 2 Upgraded Models variant How To Play A turn consists of: 1. Adding a tile to your city and placing the matching buildings onto it 2. Optionally building one or more walkways 3. Drawing a new tile from the row or the deck Adding a Tile The new tile must be placed alongside another Tile can be rotated Your city must be a 3x3 square (or a 3x4 rectangle if playing Rectangle City variant) Buildings are automatically placed on the new tile. Build Walkways Walkways score the number of points printed on them (which is NOT the length of the walkway). A walkway is placed by clicking on the space between buildings where the walkway will go. Walkway placement rules are • Only two walkways per building • Walkways must be perpendicular to the building (no diagonals) • Walkways can't be placed over empty spots (where there is no tile yet) • Walkways at various levels may go over / under other walkways but two walkways at the same level may not cross Note: The total number of walkways available are listed at the bottom of your board. These walkways are shared by all players, so as players use walkways the total number available diminish. For example: If there are three 6 piece walkways, and player A uses one then only two are remaining for all players. It is possible for one player to use all three leaving none for the other player. Drawing a Tile You can pick a new tile from the row of 3 face up tiles OR take a random one off the stack. Upgraded Models variant Game can be played with one or two special scoring cards (randomly picked at the beginning of the game): • Most Valuable Route - Find the most valuable route in your city on one of two levels (River or Forest) . A route corresponds to a connection of several buildings to each other, using walkways. Add the value of all the walkways that make up your most valuable route. Compare that route to those of other players. Player with most valuable route scores 6 points. In the event of a tie, players involved earn 3 points each. • Most Separate Routes - Count the number of separate routes built in your city. The player who built the most earns 6 points. In the event of a tie, players involved earn 3 points each. • Varied Routes - Earn 6 points if you built a route that includes at least 4 walkways of different lengths (1,2,3,5,8) OR earn 8 points if you have managed to create a route that includes the 5 walkways lengths. Each player can only earn this once. • Circuits - Earn 3 points for each circuit you have. A circuit is a closed route. • Blue buildings on the hill - Earn 6 points if you are the player with the most blue buildings. In the event of a tie, players involved earn 3 points each. • Green buildings on the hill - Earn 6 points if you are the player with the most green buildings. In the event of a tie, players involved earn 3 points each. • Minimalist Buildings - Earn 2 points per building with only one walkway built from it. • Crossed Walkways - Lose 2 points for each of your walkways that crosses another. Passing over buildings doesn't count as a crossing (even if walkways are connected to those buildings). Each walkway will count only once, even if it's crossing multiple walkways. • Solo Buildings - Lose 2 points for each building with no walkways. • Balanced Walkways - Lose 4 points if you do not have at least: 5 walkways worth 3 points, 1 walkway worth 1 point, 1 walkway worth 8 points. [Rating: 2/10] [ImageID=5528619small] A bland optimization of your personal area.  [b]Pros:[/b] It's got a captivating table presence.  [b]Cons:[/b] There's absolutely no meaningful player interaction. The one aspect where you do affect other players is by taking something from the open draft or if the different bridges run out, and that's extremely ancillary.  The puzzle itself is pedestrian, either the tiles you need come out when you need them or they don't. Not getting in your own way isn't challenging or interesting.   The physicality of it is fiddly. [Rating: 2/10] Very lacking in player interaction, and your own personal puzzle isn't that satisfying.

[Rating: 3/10] Ugly and uninspired.  I don't understand why something this generic needs to exist, in a world where there are thousands of board games.

[Rating: 3/10] This game is all about the components. Erecting buildings and laying walkways creates a compelling visual. The game itself doesn't rise to the same quality. At its heart, Cloud City is a race to securing high value walkways since each length is limited, but without anything else to focus on or compete over the experience is far too shallow.

[Rating: 3/10] Got it from a Maldito Games loot box. It's just ok. Simple game, not thrilling. It's actualy not possible to "play better" than other players. Played it with my 12 yo nephew while he was on the phone cause he was bored and he won the game anyways. Just walk away from this game.

[Rating: 3/10] If the board game market was not so good this game would probably rank higher, but its too quick, the turns feel too bland, For a game that only gives you eight turns it should not take this long. It just isn't that good. And PWH is an amazing designer and it feels like this concept was born in the bad news bears expansion to barenpark and they wanted to make a full game around it. But it isn't worth the shelf space.

[Rating: 3/10] Előkészítése és elpakolása borzalmas és semmi különlegesség nincs ebben a játékban csak a kinézete és a műanyag tornyok.

[Rating: 4/10] Kind of fun to play a couple times. I didn't see all the end game goals, but as is, replayability is on the low side. I feel the game becomes a race to place bridges before the stock disappears and less a chill building game. Bridge limits are more annoyance than reward for tactics. Oh, all that size bridge is gone? Go twiddle your thumbs while I try to find a new location for my tile.
